chunks: Amr bin Khalid bin Farrookh al-Harrani narrated: Zuhayr bin Muawiya narrated to us, saying: Ziyad bin Khaythama narrated to us, from al-Aswad bin Sa'id al-Hamadani, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This Umma will remain upright, prevailing over its enemy, until twelve Caliphs pass away, all of them from Quraysh.' When he returned to his home, delegations of Quraysh came to him and asked: 'Then what will happen?' He said: 'Commotion (Harj) will occur.' And he said: Zuhayr bin Muawiya narrated to us, saying: Ziyad bin Khaythama narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Aswad bin Sa'id al-Hamadani, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, and mentioned a similar narration.

key_terms.أَمْرُهَا: her affair/state (referring to the Umma's condition)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say would happen after the twelve caliphs from Quraysh?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, serves as a foundational text for the concept of the twelve legitimate successors, with Shia tradition specifically identifying the twelfth as the Mahdi. The mention of 'Harj' (commotion) following their reign underscores the eschatological transition from the era of the Imams to the period of occultation and eventual global justice. Its inclusion in Sunni sources alongside Shia narration highlights the shared historical expectation of Qurayshi leadership before the rise of major tribulations.
